raw_tweets.text:
An AI just read a stranger's mind through their skull, no surgery, no implants, and got roughly 45% of the meaning right on the first try. On a person it had never seen before.

That's the tech an OpenAI researcher just quit her job for. Two weeks ago she walked out of the hottest company on earth to join Conduit, a startup collecting brain recordings in a San Francisco basement.

Here's what happens in that basement. Paid volunteers put on four pound headsets covered in sensors and chat with an AI for two hours while it listens to their neurons fire. The signal is so faint the team shut off wall power to the entire building and runs on battery packs, because the hum from an ordinary outlet drowns out a human thought.

They've collected 10,000 hours of brains so far. The largest dataset of its kind ever assembled. And here's the part that should make your hands sweat. Whisper needed 680,000 hours of audio to master speech. The moment someone scales brain data the same way, the decoding stops being 45% right.

She says we're in the GPT-2 era of mind reading. GPT-2 was a joke in 2019. Five years later half the internet was written by its grandchildren.

Her timeline says developers wear thought-streaming headbands by 2027. By 2035, AI stops feeling like a tool and starts feeling like a limb.

Your inner monologue has been the one place nothing could touch for 300,000 years of human history. That run is ending in a basement in San Francisco, two hours at a time.

My average day before ChatGPT Voice:

1. Wake up
2. Sit at my desk for 10+ hours
3. Try to get outside before the sun goes down (rarely happens)
4. Be disgustingly pale

My day after ChatGPT Voice:

1. Wake up
2. Go for walk w airpods in
3. Tell Voice all my priorities for the day
4. They all get done in parallel
5. I brain dump everything else on my mind
6. Get dozens of more tasks done I didn't even think of
7. Spend maybe 15 minutes at my desk at the end of the day to check it all over
8. Go to sleep golden tan with all my work complete

I feel COMPLETELY unshackled from my desk now

I know it sounds like I'm getting paid by OpenAI, but I promise you I'm now

I'm just in serious shock more people aren't talking about this new tech

It's changed the way I work more than any other tool I've used in my life. I'm now free to work from anywhere and get SOO much more done

Do yourself a favor and challenge yourself to not work at your desk tomorrow. Do EVERYTHING from outside

Just make sure your ChatGPT app is in remote mode to your desktop. Then open up Voice and blabber about everything you need to get done.

I promise you it'll just get done

raw_tweets.text:
I made a page-flipping sketchbook inspired by Matthew Yu's concept.

Books and pages are some of the most interesting UIs to explore. AI gives you the basics unless you hand it a solid open-source to work from.

So I asked for drag to paginate, which took many fixes for shadows, clipping, alpha masks and logic. Then a magnifying glass that has to move out of the way when you flip a page.

For images I used gpt image 2 and it's very good at these Singapore sketches.

I also love adding minimal background textures like japanese paper, water painting and ornaments. That's where the personality comes from.

FYI I'm using Claude Code on the desktop app. My Codex is utterly out of limits after GPT 5.6 Sol ate all my $200/m plan 2-3x faster than 5.5. From testing, Opus 5 at Extra is more efficient.

Let me know if I should open-source this or give the prompts.
